speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you tell me when the newborn first started vomiting, and was the vomit definitely green or bilious? Also, has the baby passed any stool yet, and if so, what did it look like?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, 3050-g (6-lb 12-oz) male, six hours post delivery. The newborn has had several episodes of bilious vomiting and is intolerant to feeding since birth. Was born at term following an uncomplicated pregnancy, though the mother missed several prenatal checkups. The patient's older brother underwent surgery for pyloric stenosis as an infant.

speaker: Doctor
text: I understand the vomiting began immediately after birth, but did the baby pass any meconium stool within the first 24 hours, and does the abdomen appear distended? REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_X-Ray.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Bilious vomiting. I also have Feeding intolerance, No fever, Vomiting started within first day after birth.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on the immediate onset of bilious vomiting and feeding intolerance, I need to clarify if the infant has passed any meconium stool yet, as a complete absence would suggest distal obstruction. Has there been any abdominal distension noted by the nursing staff or parents? REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_X-Ray.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Abdominal X-ray findings show a 'double bubble' sign indicative of duodenal atresia.

speaker: Doctor
text: The abdominal X-ray findings of a 'double bubble' sign are classic for duodenal atresia, a condition often associated with this presentation. Given the clear radiographic evidence and clinical picture of bilious vomiting since birth, I have sufficient information to proceed. DIAGNOSIS READY: Duodenal Atresia.
